metadata.goal: Study the driving and task-acceptance behavior of five drivers using their multiple provided trajectories.
metadata.dataset_description: Twelve completed tasks are provided for each of five Porto taxi drivers. The data include task order, local origin and destination coordinates, timestamps, driver shifts, long idle windows, taxi-stand locations, and timestamped route points.

insight_list.insight: Most drivers complete tasks within one service area before moving to the next area; for example, they spend an extended sequence in the west before transitioning eastward to continue accepting tasks.

insight_list.question: Do drivers generally finish a local sequence of tasks before moving to another service area?

insights: Most drivers complete tasks within one service area before moving to the next area; for example, they spend an extended sequence in the west before transitioning eastward to continue accepting tasks.
Drivers commonly experience extended idle windows after completing a batch of consecutive tasks.
During these idle windows, the drivers usually, though not always, wait at a taxi stand.
The five drivers begin work at different times, but each works for approximately ten hours.
summary: Across the five drivers, completed tasks are predominantly organized as consecutive within-area sequences before a transition to the next service area. Their workloads contain extended idle windows between consecutive task batches; most of these windows are spent at a taxi stand. Despite staggered starts, the five shifts are all close to ten hours long.
